title: Foot care in diabetes
also: how to care for your feet with diabetes
what: With diabetes, the feet feel pain less and small wounds heal more slowly. Daily care helps prevent foot ulcers.
why: For everyone with diabetes, every day.
tell_doctor: If your feet go numb, burn, or feel cold
If calluses, cracks, or sores appeared
If the color of your skin or nails changed
If it is hard to examine your feet yourself

prepare.title: Light and mirror
prepare.text: Check your feet in good light. A mirror makes it easy to see the sole.

prepare.title: Shoes
prepare.text: Soft, the right size, with no hard seams inside. Before putting them on, check with your hand for pebbles.

prepare.title: Helper
prepare.text: If you cannot see well or it is hard to bend, ask a family member to check your feet.

steps: Check your feet every day: soles, toes, and between the toes
Wash your feet in warm water, and test the temperature with your hand or a thermometer
Dry them well, especially between the toes
Apply cream to your feet, but not between the toes
File your nails straight across and do not cut the corners
Wear clean socks without tight elastic
Do not walk barefoot, even at home
feel: If feeling is reduced, you may not notice a sore, which is why checking matters
Dry skin and cracks are common, and cream helps
after: Do not warm your feet with a heating pad or soak them in hot water, since you can easily burn them
Do not cut calluses or ingrown nails yourself, see a doctor
Show your feet to your doctor regularly at visits
red_flags: A sore, ulcer, or crack that does not heal in a few days
Redness, swelling, pus, or a bad smell
The foot became cold, pale, or blue
A fever and severe pain in the leg

faq.a: Yes, from a technician who knows about diabetes, without sharp tools. A medical pedicure is better.
You can hurt yourself and not notice. With diabetes, such a wound heals slowly.

reminders.text: This evening, check your feet: toes, soles, and between the toes.
